📚 Today you learned

The Wash Sale Rule

Sell a stock at a loss and buy the same or a "substantially identical" security within 30 days before or after, and the IRS disallows the loss — it rolls into the new lot's cost basis instead of being deductible now. Forex has nothing like it; this is US tax law, not a broker restriction, though IBKR will flag it on your 1099-B. It only bites losses, never gains, and it doesn't block the trade itself — you can re-enter immediately, you just can't claim the loss on that year's taxes yet. Not relevant to SPXC specifically, since the cash math points to a small profit there, not a loss. But the next time a stop takes a real loss on a name you still like, know the 31-day window before you refile straight back into it.

Also today: Cost basis step-up on a wash sale — the disallowed loss doesn't disappear, it defers: it gets added to the replacement lot's basis, so you recover it (as a smaller future gain or bigger future loss) whenever that lot eventually closes.
